concerns.text: T006 is too coarse for deterministic execution: one task bundles (a) simulation-based power analysis with sensitivity sweep, (b) VIF diagnostic with gate flag, (c) two MixedLM fits with convergence retry, and (d) a Gamma GLMM / log-transform fallback. Each sub-part has distinct inputs, code files (model_fit.py, lmm_power.py, vif_calc.py), and verification criteria. Split so each gate/model artifact is independently verifiable.

T003 bundles DeepGaze II batched inference, GBVS fallback with validation rules, resource tracking with psutil, resource_validator.py implementation, smoke run, and salience_stats.json gate logic into one task. The atomizer should split at least the resource-validator module and the fallback/exclusion logic from the core inference.

T004 bundles two modules (segment_roi.py with YOLOv8 + SCR-002 exclusion logging, parse_fixations.py with three metrics) plus two test files. Splitting into segmentation and fixation-parsing tasks would make each verification (mask artifacts vs fixations.csv) independently checkable.

T006(b) is plausibly unexecutable as specified: SCR-001's rationale predicts VIF > 5 between salience and the low-level features ('Including both creates high multicollinearity (VIF > 5)'), yet T006(b) halts the entire pipeline when VIF > 5. If the plan's own prediction holds, the pipeline halts before producing lmm_results.csv, so T006's verification ('results CSV contains the salience fixed effect') can never be satisfied. Root cause is the spec/plan gate semantics (VIF>5 should trigger a documented decision, not a hard halt given SCR-001 already excludes the covariates); needs resolution before the task is executable.
